name: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485)

requirement_groups.name: Post-Study Work stream (bachelor's degree or higher)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires having completed a bachelor's degree, master's degree, or doctorate from an Australian institution.
This requires being under 35 at the time of application — a genuine age-limit reform introduced as part of recent policy changes.
This requires a qualification linked to an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list, plus a positive skills assessment.

evidence_required.document: Degree certificate from the Australian institution

outcome.duration_length: duration varies by qualification level (commonly 18 months to 2-4 years for Post-Study Work stream depending on degree level; 18 months for Graduate Work stream) — recent reforms shortened some durations and added the age-35 limit

sources.title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) - Department of Home Affairs

notes: SOURCING CAVEAT flagged honestly: recent reforms shortened Post-Study Work stream durations for some qualification levels and introduced a new age-35 cap (down from an older, higher limit) — the exact current duration-by-degree-level table was not fully confirmed at tier-1 precision during this research pass and should be re-verified against the current immi.homeaffairs.gov.au page before treating the duration_length figures here as final. Full, unrestricted work rights during the visa period — genuinely more generous than several other countries' post-study routes in this dataset. Direct feeder into Australia's skilled-visa ecosystem (482, 189, 190), closing Australia's version of the core Journey chain, though notably NOT itself leading to PR/citizenship — matching the terminal, must-convert-before-expiry pattern seen in UK Graduate, Germany's Job Seeker permit, and the Netherlands' Orientation Year.
